By the way, is it just me or is his lady friend kind of an a-hole? His best friend just died and she's grilling him for being a quitter! Jeez, maybe give him some time to figure his sh*t out, seriously!

Recommended for those that enjoy the DANGER ZONE!, hot shot renegade pilots who live by their own rules, by-the-book authority figures, super cool-guy nicknames, cheesy 80's soundtracks, gender neutral bathrooms, sweaty shirtless man sports, spinning horizons, macho staring contests, spontaneously breaking out into song, slow-mo erotic mouth licking, intense bro-hugs...

...but that's just like, my opinion, man

# Of Times Watched: Once

4.title: Cruise at his cockiest
4.content:
For unfathomable reasons this was a mega hit in the 80s. Cruise is at his most insufferable as the perennially grinning Maverick, an undisciplined fight pilot who wants to be the best.

That's it. Basically there's no plot, apart from a flimsy background story of Maverick's dad, also an ace pilot deceased in Vietnam and an unconvincing romance between Maverick and "astrophysics" instructor Charlie.

Undoubtedly the photography and some of the fight scenes are impressive, but shallow. The bunch of pilots populating the movie barely seem real, they all look like male models of the 80s, muscled, tanned and cocky.

Not that I mind movies that display very watchable young male flesh, but unfortunately apart from voyeurism the supporting cast (headed by Val Kilmer) offers little originality in the roles of best buddy, antagonist and antagonist's buddy, plus wise older man.

Some mention the soundtrack as plus point, but I found it grating, with far too much 80s synthesizers and the insufferably cheesy "Takes my breath away".

4.title: Colonel Bogey
4.content:
With the long gestating sequel now ready to be relased, I thought it about time I watched the original, which has somehow eluded me for the last 30 years. I wasn't expecting much, given the reputation of the movie, but even I was surprised at the lack of story and how boring the dogfighting scenes were.

Pete 'Maverick' Mitchell (Tom Cruise) is a fighter pilot, who together with his second, Nick 'Goose' Bradshaw (Anthony Edwards) heads to the Navy's elite training program codenamed "Top Gun". Though undoubtably a skilled pilot, Maverick struggles to follow orders and his instructors and fellow pilots find him unreliable. Whilst at 'Top Gun" he begins a relationship with intelligence officer Charlotte Blackwood (Kelly McGillis) but repeated insubordination hampers his chances of progression.

I didn't like it, is the considered opinion after this first watch. Apologies again if this film has been in your life for years and you truly love it, but it's a weird mishmash of minor plots that never amount to a consistent story. Ideally, Mitchell should learn a lesson based on his own arrogance that teaches him to be part of a team. He doesn't though, as the incident that occurs isn't his fault and subsequently, he doesn't seem to act any different. But I'd heard the rep before that the film was largely plotless, so I was prepared for that. What I wasn't prepared for was how boring the film's dogfighting scenes were going to be. Mostly they take place as part of the training, so there is no firing involved. It's just endless shots of people spinning their heads around inside the cockpits trying to spot their bogeys.

It's not entirely irredeemable. Tom Cruise is as watchable as always, there are some Iconic scenes, such as the "You've lost that loving feeling" moment and the volleyball scene.

It's perhaps the ultimate style of substance film, and given the style has been replicated so much since, even that's not much of a plus point anymore.

4.title: Towel time
4.content:
How had i never seen this? The cultural references are well ingrained in me.

The script is hammy nonsense, it's homoerotic to eleven; but rollickingly good fun.

4.title: At its best when it is high up in the sky
4.content:
Lieutenant Pete 'Maverick' Mitchell and his best friend Goose are accepted into an elite flying school (one which only the top 1% are eligible to enter). Upon arriving at what is known as 'Top Gun' Maverick finds himself at loggerheads with ace pilot Iceman, romancing instructor Charlie as well as being haunted by memories of his father...

Tony Scott is an action director and it's fair to say that he has done the best that he can with Top Gun based on what he had to work with. The scenes up in the sky have some intensity about them and its these scenes that give the film a kind of semi-watchability; although even the best action director can only do so much to make the spectacle of planes flying around exciting before things start to become repetitive and the novelty begins to wear off.

It's when you start to look at everything that occurs on the ground in Top Gun where the film runs into big problems; for starters there isn't a great deal of story, the characters just aren't engaging and the romance between Maverick and Charlie is quite simply unbelievable. Maverick has demons involving his father which could have made his character and his journey as a top gun pilot a damn site more interesting had this been explored better.

The acting is a bit of a mixed bag; Edwards and McGillis are both OK (without being great). Kilmer and Cruise are the 'pretty cast members' who trade insults and smile a lot, but contribute little else...then again were they really asked to do anything else here? Veteran actors such as Skerritt and Ironside add a bit of a class and feel like they are too good for this film.

I really liked this film when I was younger and one senses that the target audience is teenagers, but as someone who is now in their late 30's it just doesn't appeal to me all that much now. It's hollow, shallow and superficial with only some of the scenes high up in the sky providing a modicum of entertainment.

4.title: It did not take my breath away
4.content:
OK, I will never ever split movies into like a "Chick Flick" or "Guy's flick" category. I hate it when people do that. But for the first time ever, it seemed like such a macho guy flick. I love romantic movies, so I asked my mom and friend what was the most romantic movie they ever saw and they said "Top Gun". I knew we had it, so I watched it. The only thing I loved about it was the sexy Tom Cruise and Val Kilmer. Other than that, I'd skip it.

4/10

4.title: Product of the times
4.content: I won't argue that this movie was probably great when it was released, but it has not stood up to the test of time. This is such a corny movie with a boring plot: boy meets girl, which turns out to be his commander, romance, volleyball, planes, the end. Not very captivating and is very simply a corny romance movie with planes. Could have been told in any other situation in hundreds of different ways, and it has been, i'm not sure why this movie is seen as great by everyone. Maverick was a fantastic sequel, and if you want my opinion, skip this movie and just watch Maverick.

4.content:

4.title: Barely a movie, Military Propaganda
4.content:
It's barely a movie - the plot is nonsensical - mostly just a montage of cool fighter jet aviation shots mixed to music.

There's a lot of one liner and 80s style make out scenes, but very little story. Worse, this movie was financed and edited by the American military - it's a love letter to recruitment and basically unfiltered propaganda.

4.title: MiGs? What MiGs?
4.content: What do these US film producers take us for? A film with an abysmal script and predictable plot enlivened by some very accomplished airborne photography and clever editing - not to mention skillful flying - is reduced to a cartoon film strip by Top Gun flyer's identifying F-5 Freedom Fighters as MiGs! Oh for heaven's sake... we had to resort to such tactics when we made Reach for the Sky back in the 50s, surely we don't have to do it now. Having flown in the Royal Air Force for forty years, I can vouch for the fact that the average USAF jock's aircraft recognition skills can be suspect at times - to say the least! But the Best of the Best (Oh Really!) shouldn't be seen splashing F-5s!! It's bad for morale. I suppose any old jet will do, as long as they look different from Tomcats, their pilots have got black bone domes and look vaguely foreign.

4.title: Masculinity Covering Over a Void of Actual Story or Meaningful World Building
4.content:
Largely exploited as promotional material to join the US Air Force, Top Gun displays a rather strange and uninteresting representation of reality. Garnering a group of overly ambitious pilots, the film tries to project them as courageous and bright young men.

However most of the film is steeped with tedious romantic filler and pointless scenes with messy cinematography. It almost wants to be a slice of life drama rather than a serious action movie, and it serrates the overall mixture where the whole movie feels like a rough cut.

The climax should have be an exciting finale, however the dogfights were too ambitious for the time to be entertaining, and the enemy is so indistinctive and meaningless that I simply didn't care for any of it.
